subject.title: fix(slack): repeated external menus grow gateway memory

question: Is silently evicting a still-unexpired Slack external menu at a gateway-wide limit of 256 an acceptable supported overflow behavior?
rationale: The cap prevents retention growth, but it changes the observable ten-minute menu-availability contract for busy workspaces; source and unit coverage cannot choose the intended user-facing degradation policy or capacity.

options.title: Adopt the bounded LRU policy
options.body: Approve 256-entry LRU eviction as the supported overload behavior after adding clear real-world proof that it is safe for expected concurrent Slack menu usage.

options.title: Preserve live-menu availability
options.body: Revise the overflow path so users receive a deliberate recoverable Slack result rather than an indistinguishable expired-menu response when a valid menu is evicted.

options.title: Pause for channel-owner design
options.body: Hold the PR until the Slack owner selects a capacity and recovery model for high-concurrency external menus.

recommendation.title: Preserve live-menu availability
recommendation.body: Revise the overflow path so users receive a deliberate recoverable Slack result rather than an indistinguishable expired-menu response when a valid menu is evicted.
